correctness.rationale: I reconstructed the unrestricted proof. With A the adjacency matrix, A²=(v−1)I/4−A+(v−1)J/4 and AJ=(v−1)J/2, so S=2A+I−J gives S²=vI−J. Expanding the indicator of an allowed sign triple modulo simultaneous negation gives (1+t_a t_b s_ax s_bx+t_a t_c s_ax s_cx+t_b t_c s_bx s_cx)/4. Summing and subtracting the third anchor's contribution gives the stated (s_e+τ)ε_e terms. Each is at most 2, and triangles exist at every admissible v≥9 and attain the bound for all-positive requests. Every pair has both signs at all v≥5. These extension properties maintain partial isomorphisms after arbitrary pebble reuses (including copying a surviving anchor for equality), not merely fresh moves. At v=5 every four-set is a path. At v=9 the triangles form a cubic triangle-free auxiliary graph on six vertices, necessarily K3,3, giving the rook graph. In it (1,1),(1,2),(2,3),(3,3) is an induced pair of disjoint edges, hence an all-positive four-set; a triangle admits no all-positive fourth point. This gives the two rank-four separators, whereas rank-three sentences can rename bound variables with only three live names. The least representative orders are within the conference-graph family under review. After at most (v−13)/4 deletions, three-anchor extensions still exist; with at least 13 vertices surviving, requests over fewer anchors may also be padded to three. Deleting exactly the (v−9)/4 witnesses of an all-positive triangle request preserves the anchors and makes the rank-four obstruction true. The recorded Paley cases are checks, not premises of the proof.
